entries.mandate: Show why metal building professionals can trust a longtime accessory manufacturer whose value lives in repeatable process, product consistency, and people who know the work.
entries.execution: The film blends executive interviews, historical photos, ribbon-cutting texture, shop-floor cutting and forming, paint/finishing detail, training-room context, facility scale, and finished goods in transit.
entries.outcome: A sales-facing company overview that makes the operation feel established, specific, and current: a family-rooted manufacturer with modern process proof and a clear place in the metal building supply chain.

entries.title: Kappa Rap 2
entries.scope: Baylor Kappa Kappa Gamma recruitment video, long-tail YouTube and convention-use legacy
entries.headline: A recruitment music video that outgrew rush and became Baylor lore.
entries.summary: Created in 2011 for Kappa Kappa Gamma at Baylor, Kappa Rap 2 turned a chapter recruitment idea into a campus-culture artifact. The video kept resurfacing across Greek-life circles and social platforms, drew renewed press interest around its RushTok-era afterlife, and surpassed 1.4M YouTube views.
entries.mandate: Translate the Baylor Kappas' original song and chapter energy into a video students would share, quote, and remember after recruitment week ended.
entries.execution: Bailey Eubanks directed a bright, personality-forward edit around the three credited creators, the Baylor Kappas, white-background performance setups, neon classroom choreography, campus walk-throughs, and fast chorus repetition that made the hook easy to retain.
entries.outcome: The piece became more than a rush-room asset: it earned a Baylor Lariat retrospective, prompted national-media interest, and remained useful enough that the creators requested the full-resolution file in 2026 for national Kappa convention playback.
